newsitem.title: USA: Clinton policies seen factor in high lumber prices.
newsitem.headline: Clinton policies seen factor in high lumber prices.

text.p: Lumber producers in the United States have been hampered in their response to rising prices by government policies which restrict access to federal forests, a trade association executive said.

Robert Hunt, president of the Western Wood Products Association, said lumber prices have increased by more than 30 percent since the first of the year as demand for wood has expanded. However, producers have found it difficult to respond to the increased demand as they have in the past.
"American home buyers and other lumber users are paying the price for the Clinton administration's short-sighted timber harvesting policies," he said in a news release.
"This market illustrates what happens when you lock away forests from multiple uses and limit the Western industry's ability to meet the country's wood product needs," he said.

Hunt noted that home builders and others have criticized a U.S.-Canadian lumber trade agreement for increasing prices. He said other issues such as timber harvesting restrictions had influenced prices as much, if not more, than Canadian quotas.
Since 1987, harvests from federal forests in the western United States have fallen 78 percent. Hunt said it was unlikely they would re-emerge as a major timber source in the near future.
